Definition: Whether government taxes, customs duties, and other revenue can be paid using the instant digital payment system, indicating integration of payment infrastructure with tax administration systems.
Comments: Evidence not fully researched in this subagent run. Located evidence of a digital-only mandate for settling tax payments (zero-cash-handling policy) alongside e-filing, implying revenue collection via digital channels; however did not extract ERS primary source describing payment channels in time.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: Verified: ERS payment pages (2025) show EFT, mobile money, POS and bank-deposit channels cover both domestic taxes and customs & excise duties, and a zero-cash-handling mandate has applied to ERS offices since April 2021. An ICTD working paper (Santoro et al., 2025) confirms cash's share of tax transactions fell from 36% (2018) to 2% (2021) under this mandate. Coverage is comprehensive across tax and duty types, so upgraded from Partial (2) to Yes (3).

Definition: Whether the system enables citizen payments to government for taxes, fees, licenses, fines, utility bills, and other government service charges.
Comments: Eswatini has digitised person-to-government payments for some services: “Government in Your Hand” app enables paying for vehicle licences via mobile money, indicating P2G capability for at least some government fees.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The original insidebiz.co.sz URL is now dead/hijacked (resolves to an unrelated betting-site page) and could not be verified. Corroborated via ITWeb Africa (22 May 2025) that the Government-in-Your-Hand app lets citizens pay vehicle licences by mobile money, register business names and access services, alongside ERS's mandatory zero-cash-handling policy (since April 2021) that already makes digital P2G tax payment near-universal for taxpayers. Combined, this is active rather than merely limited P2G use, so upgraded from Limited Use (2) to Yes - Active Use (3).

Definition: Whether and how the central bank participates in payment system governance beyond its regulatory oversight role, including board representation, operational management, technical standard-setting, or direct system operation.
Comments: The Central Bank of Eswatini (CBE) directly operates EPS (“fully financed and operated by the Central Bank of Eswatini; all hardware, software and processes are hosted within its purview”), indicating direct operational governance.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: The cited FAQ page was fetched and only covers banknotes/coins/ATM dye packs — it does not mention the payment system and does not support the claim. However, better primary sources confirm the underlying score: the SWIPSS Rules & Procedures state 'the SWIPSS system is owned and operated by the Central Bank,' and the CBE-Cenfri CBDC Diagnostic (2021) confirms SWIPSS is 'owned, managed and located within the CBE,' serving the Treasury directly. Direct Operation (5) is confirmed on these sources; the original citation should be replaced as it does not support the score.

Definition: Percentage of the adult population (15+ years) who have made at least one digital payment transaction through the instant payment system in the past 90 days, indicating active usage rather than just account ownership.
Comments: FinScope Eswatini 2018 (FinMark Trust) reports ~66% of adults made digital payments in the past 12 months (about 460k adults), implying 50–69% active digital payment users.
redteam_note: Only one source for a substantive score — corroborate.
revision_notes: FinScope 2018 (66% of adults, 12-month digital payment) is dated. Eswatini's National Financial Inclusion Strategy 2023-2028 (Ministry of Finance/CFI, verified) cites 71% of adults using mobile money with 'uptake continues to grow' and E18bn+ in annual mobile-money transaction value, which would sit in the 70-89% band rather than 50-69%. However, no source gives a precise 90-day 'active user' figure (as distinct from broader account use/ownership), so the exact banding is ambiguous. Keeping the original 50-69% score but flagging for human review given corroborating evidence that current usage may now exceed 69%.
